rubric.evidence: IDL transcribed verbatim from the editor's draft fetched 2026-09-13 (HeadersInit headers = {} in WebTransportOptions; [SameObject] readonly attribute Headers? responseHeaders) and cross-checked against the PR #713 diff fetched from patch-diff.githubusercontent.com. Constructor processing (fill from options["headers"], request-guarded append, wt-available-protocols TypeError, forbidden-header note) and the connection-established steps (copy response header list, delete wt-protocol, immutable guard) were transcribed from spec section 6.2. Spec prose for both members is quoted verbatim and marked as such. Flag names (enable-experimental-web-platform-features, WebTransportHeaders runtime + Finch) come from the ChromeStatus record, the Intent to Ship, and a direct fetch of runtime_enabled_features.json5.

Slug webtransport-headers-and-responseheaders is the slugified milestone=153 LISTING name 'WebTransport headers and responseHeaders'; the feature id 5194104408506368 was confirmed in the milestone=153 features_by_type under 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)' by direct API query 2026-09-13. The same id's appearance in the milestone=155 listing under 'Enabled by default' is disclosed honestly on the page (warn-block and compat table) while the page documents the dev-trial state at 153.

The feature adds exactly two developer-facing surface items (spec PR #713 diff read in full); both are inventoried in reference-contract.json and mapped to dedicated child routes with all nine dimensions covered (responseHeaders uses a sourced not-applicable for inputs, being a readonly attribute). Error paths include the non-obvious silent-drop of forbidden request-headers versus the throwing wt-available-protocols case; lifecycle covers population timing relative to ready, failure, and post-close behavior.

why-it-exists explains the three concrete workarounds this replaces (tokens in query strings leaking to logs, extra round trip over a data stream, gateways unable to route at the CONNECT layer) from the ChromeStatus motivation, plus the WG provenance (issue #263, PR #713, TPAC 2025 consensus). The wt-protocol/protocol relationship and the no-CORS-preflight rationale are spelled out. Not a 5: the interaction with connection pooling (allowPooling) and headers is not addressed by the spec or intent and is only implicitly covered.

Overview shows feature detection, bearer auth + codec negotiation end-to-end, and all three HeadersInit forms; the headers child page adds both TypeError paths and the silent forbidden-header drop as runnable snippets; the responseheaders child page covers null-before-ready, guaranteed-populated-after-ready, immutability TypeError, and the failure path. Honest limitation stated in citations: snippets are source-derived, not runtime-executed, because no flag-enabled Chrome 153 plus opted-in WebTransport server was available to this writer.

Real BCD entry api.WebTransport.responseHeaders cited from the fetched raw file (chrome false, firefox false, safari preview, experimental); the missing BCD subfeature for the headers option is disclosed and those rows are labelled interim with primary-source evidence. Chrome rows separate the 153 dev-trial state from the slated 155 default-on state with listing links for each. Fallback guidance (feature detection via 'responseHeaders' in WebTransport.prototype, query-param/app-level handshake fallback) comes from the Intent to Ship.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing and the browser's layout engine; wrap potentially-wide content in overflow containers; use flex-wrap whenever overflow is possible; never mask layout issues with overflow:hidden.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every doc/compat table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede, code and table cells; <wbr> inside the long member-name H1s; .baseline-browsers is a flex row with wrap; pre blocks scroll internally rather than widening the page. Exception: no container queries - the shared single-column editorial measure fits the reference format (same as accepted exemplar pages).

guidanceConsulted.query: semantic accessible code examples pre code blocks documentation page
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic HTML structures (real tables with header cells, landmarks, correct heading order); code belongs in <pre><code>; give non-text signal blocks roles/labels.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: all examples are semantic <pre><code>; data tables use th scope=row (and thead for columnar tables); the baseline banner carries role=note with an aria-label; heading order is strict h1>h2>h3; external links are labelled by their visible text rather than bare URLs.
